Let's split the wrapper for ObjectMapper into a separate class and use the opportunity to get rid of the related inline callbacks.

ObjectMapper is a fairly standard dependency and we do not need to mix it up with any other functionality.
I created ObjectMapper and InventoryManager class in follow up changes.

I assume that's a dataflow diagram.

Can we restructure the diagram to visualize how the code would work with this patch, at the current stage of development.

Because currently we do not have `InventoryManager` class.
See follow up change.
leftover semicolon 😄
Done

Why `unique_ptr`, is it reset anywhere?

From how it's initialized in the constructor, it can be a regular class member variable, right?
Made it a shared_ptr.

That's not what i meant. Usually people prefer `regular member variable`, `unique_ptr`, `shared_ptr`, in that order.

Regular member variable is easiest to reason about since it is valid during the entire lifetime of the object which holds it. `unique_ptr` is less desirable because we may need to check if it's there (can be `nullptr`).

`shared_ptr` is something of a last resort, when other representations cannot represent the use-case.

Since there is only one instance of `SystemMapper` and it is constructed in `EntityManager` constructor, it can be a regular member variable.

Which is convenient since we never need to check for `nullptr`.

There is also some performance issue with `shared_ptr` since it does reference counting.

https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/memory/shared_ptr.html (Implementation Notes Section)
I think I figured it out 😄

Since `ObjectMapper` interaction is separate from what `SystemMapper` is doing,
what do you think about first extracting some class to abstract away the `ObjectMapper` usage and use that opportunity to get rid of these inline callbacks.

Then at the next patch introduce `SystemMapper` class.

Creating a seprarate class for ObjectMapper interaction is something I can get behind. Getting rid of the inline lamdas would be a temporary step, until I move the project to sdbusplus::async, hence I dont see much value in that. GetSubTree and getInterface functions will be very short with sdbusplus::async, like less than 20LoCs. 

Further more, i would have to pass the reference to dbusProbeObjects into this class, which I want to avoid.

> Further more, i would have to pass the reference to dbusProbeObjects into this class, which I want to avoid.

Why? You can just have a `std::bind_front` to bind the arguments to whichever callback you pass into the wrapper for object mapper.

> GetSubTree and getInterface functions will be very short with sdbusplus::async, like less than 20LoCs. 

Yes, small and well-defined functions. We do not have to create a class but a namespace could work. It reduces the visual noise from having mapper-specific bus names and object path literals inside code that's only a mapper client.
Solved it without bind_front

I'm still trying to figure out how this class helps.

So, the EntityManager class serves as a general service setup, while the SystemMapper class acutally connects the different means and sources of information and processes them. If you take a look on the follow up changes in the patch train, you'll get an idea. 

In the next two changes there's a ASCII diagram about the end result im trying to reach. Over all I'll try to achieve more seperation of concern. In the end I want a state that is simple to follow data flow and have different classes each with a well scoped responsibility. Fundamental principles of software engineering basically.

Im aware that this change cannot stand for itself, the two follow up changes are required for this change to really make sense :)
